name: lens-reader
description: The /lens Reader lens: a third-party extractor's opinion of a page, served from its own Worker so the site bundle never carries a DOM.
$comment: Every wrangler script passes -c wrangler.toml EXPLICITLY. Without it wrangler walks UP the tree, finds the ROOT wrangler.jsonc, and runs its build.command (`node tools/build.ts`) from this directory, dying with MODULE_NOT_FOUND on a file that only exists at the repo root. CI's steps for cf-garage and lwe-ask have always passed -c for that reason, so the flag looks like ceremony until you drop it: `pnpm run deploy` then fails in a way no CI run can catch, because CI never invokes these scripts.
$comment:htmlparser2-override: linkedom 0.18.13 declares htmlparser2 ^10.1.0, whose v5/v3/v2 DOM stack duplicates the v6/v4/v3 stack linkedom already gets through css-select. htmlparser2 11 uses that newer stack and keeps the Parser behavior linkedom expects. Version 12 is NOT interchangeable: its WHATWG raw-text change breaks linkedom's self-closing script serialization in the upstream suite. The deliberate v11 override removes the duplicate entity tables without taking that change: 113.30 -> 80.56 KiB gzip (28.9% less), byte-identical output on a fixed four-page corpus, no measurable conversion regression, and linkedom's full upstream suite green. The Reader tests assert both behavior and the resolved single-generation graph. Re-evaluate this override, do not carry it blindly, when linkedom changes its parser range.

scripts.comment:typecheck: Runs from HERE rather than from the root `typecheck` script, because this project is deliberately out of the workspace and readability/linkedom live in lens-reader/node_modules. Wired into the root script instead, CI fails with TS2307 on both imports while every workstation that has run an install here stays green, which is the split CLAUDE.md records about the root contract suite arriving through a second door. tsc itself comes from the root install; only the dependency graph is local. The test suite is a SECOND program (config/tsconfig.lens-reader-test.json) because it runs on node while src/ runs on workerd, and it goes through check-test-types.mjs rather than tsc directly: importing ../src/reader.js pulls the Worker's crawl.ts in against node globals, and those diagnostics are missing declarations rather than findings.
